stem: Root-zone pH samples from different parts of the same container disagree consistently. What is the best response?
choices: Use the reading closest to the target because the most typical value is likely to represent the active root zone
Standardize sampling location and method, repeat measurements, and treat persistent spatial variation as useful data
Increase fertilizer strength until measurements from different container locations converge toward the same pH
Replace pH monitoring with EC measurements because conductivity is less affected by within-container sampling location
rationale: Root-zone chemistry can vary spatially. Consistent sampling and repeated measurements are needed to determine whether the difference is real and relevant to the active root zone.
